# Findings data (auto-generated by `quantlab report`)

Tuning season: 2023-24. Test seasons: 2024-25, 2025-26. All predictions walk-forward: features use earlier games only, plus the game's starting fives and who appeared (the stand-in for the inactive list; see the inactive-list section). Bold = best model per statistic before rounding (values that tie at the decimals shown are effectively level).

## Do matchup (opponent) features help? LightGBM ablation, test seasons

Nested design: the without-opponent model has no opponent style factors, the EB expectation with neutral opponent factors, and the team's own season-to-date averages in place of the team-model environment; the with-opponent model adds the opponent information back to the same features. Both are refits whose features differ from the shipped gradient-boosting model's (no recent per-minute rates; the own-team averages and the neutral-opponent expectation are kept in both), so the MAE with opponent information differs slightly from the gradient-boosting rows above. Both keep the projected minutes, whose blowout-risk features come from the team model's expected margin against this opponent.

| Stat | MAE with opponent information | MAE without | Gain | Gain (% of MAE) | 95% CI (game-clustered bootstrap) |

## Computational cost

20,000 simulated games: 1.26 s (63 µs per game, 4 cores) + 0.27 s pilot calibration. Invariants on every simulated game: points_identity, team_points_equal_score, minutes_equal_5x_game, assists_le_made_fg, makes_le_attempts, plus_minus_sums, no_ties, rebounds_reconcile_with_misses, fouls_le_6 -> all = True.
